verification_vocabulary: Same as GRAPH-FORMAT.md: bibliographic_metadata_checked = identity/edition checked against the record named; supporting_page_checked = an abstract, publisher summary, contents page, review text or opening text was read for the specific point in the note; unverified = could not be confirmed, kept out of proposed sources. No book was read in full. Subtitles follow Crossref, Open Library or the citation graph's bibliographic strings; places of publication follow publisher convention and were not separately checked.

sections.quebec: Quebec: Quiet Revolution, continuity and rupture, 1968.
sections.myth_memory: The sixties as myth and as an international moment.

records.citation: Myrna Kostash, Long Way from Home: The Story of the Sixties Generation in Canada (Toronto: James Lorimer, 1980).

verification.checked_against: Open Library work OL157230W (J. Lorimer & Co., 1980); Formac Lorimer product page (https://formaclorimerbooks.ca/product/long-way-from-home/); Donna E. Smyth, 'Interview with Myrna Kostash', Atlantis (c. 1980) (https://atlantisjournal.ca/index.php/atlantis/article/download/4669/3902); Brian Fawcett's Globe and Mail review as quoted at https://www.myrnakostash.com/book-store/long-way-from-home-review/
verification.note: Publisher copy read: the story of 'the Sixties generation--her generation--', 'based on interviews with hundreds of people who participated in the events described'. In the Atlantis interview (per answers/verification.json Q92) Kostash said 'I was never a political radical. I was just a hanger-on' and that she was never in a leadership role in SDS. Described here as an interview-based history by a member of the generation, a participant-observer on the edge of the movements; not a memoir and not a movement leader's account.

records.reading: An interview-based history of the sixties generation by a member of it (participant-observer).
